title: Microneedle-based ISF Sampling Technique
official: Clinical Investigation of the PELSA Microneedle-Based Device for Dermal Interstitial Fluid Sampling in Healthy Adults: Assessment of Performance and Safety
summary:
This clinical investigation aims to evaluate the performance and safety of the PELSA system, a hollow microneedle-based medical device designed for the collection of dermal interstitial fluid (dISF) from human skin.

Healthy adult volunteers will undergo a single dISF sampling session using the PELSA system. The primary objective is to assess the proportion of participants from whom at least 1 µL of dISF can be successfully collected during one sampling session.

Device safety and tolerability will also be evaluated, including the occurrence of adverse events, participant-reported pain, and local skin reactions. Exploratory assessments may include glucose detection and proteomic analysis of collected dISF samples.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 18-80 years of age (inclusive) at the time of ICF signature.
* Participant is willing to participate and is capable of giving informed consent.
* Participants must understand and sign the informed consent form, be able to comply with all study procedures and must be available for the duration of the study

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known dermatologic condition at the site of measurement, including active skin injury, lesion, infection or other dermatologic condition
* Pregnant or breastfeeding persons
* The participant has recently taken NSAIDS (within 72 hours of screening), Aspirin (5 days), prescription anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin, 5 days), or P2Y12 antiplatelet therapies (1 week)
* Vulnerable persons
* On persons with an open wound in or near the sampling area.
* On persons with any type of tattoo or piercing anywhere in or near the sampling area.
* On acral skin.
